posts.text: Thank you for even considering my inquiry, Yves. I apologize for not making my inquiry clearer! OK, all I am looking for is the bit stream that is emitted at GPIO 4 - but without the 38kHz modulation. Instead of having a 38kHz PF "on-bit", I just would like to get the plain "bit on/off" signal. And I would then feed this signal into the input of my 433MHz transmitters. OOK (on/off keying) is the simplest way of sending a signal to a receiver: Input bit = 1 -> send a 433MHz carrier signal, just that. There is no information stored in this signal; it is just "there". Bit = 0: Send nothing. The matching receiver (these are old LINX TX/RX modules) turns its output on, when it detects a 433MHz carrier signal, and keeps it off when there is nothing. This is the same with the TSOP modules: When they see a 38kHz IR signal, they turn their output on, when there is nothing, it remains off. So using these RF TX/RX modules, I don't need the 38kHz modulation of an on-bit, I just need the on-bit itself and feed that into the transmitter. That will modulate the on-bit (as 433MHz) signal. GPIO 4 sends on = 38kHz (on/off) signals; I would like to have a second GPIO output that just sends on = on. Does that make any sense? Best Thorsten

posts.title: DC Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: I don't think it's all that complicated- I feel like there's a simple flow of "I don't like the current universe's direction - I don't think it'd be easy to fix - I would like them to start again." 1. I don't like the current universe- I haven't liked a single DCU project (at least from the ones I've seen, and I doubt creature commandos or supergirl will sway me). They range from "ok but with some major lore changes I dislike" (superman 2025) to "I would say it feels like the writers hated the character, but it's not just how it feels, the writers have actively said some crazy stuff about the character" (Lanterns). 2. It wouldn't be easy to fix. There are some things that aren't all that major- Kal-El's family being evil is a ridiculous change but probably wouldn't have much of an impact on future stories- but others, like what they did to Hal (and John tbh) require a lot of work to get back into a good position- Hal's situation is pretty much unfixable without a truckload of retcons. Not to mention the main issues- the weird sort of semi-break from the DCEU and the resulting random (and mostly R-rated) selection of projects. When this all started Gunn said something along the lines of the reason it's not starting with Batman and Wonder Woman is because he goes with the best scripts, but... if the projects we've gotten were better scripts than anything anyone's brought him on any of the major heroes, I feel like you're having some troubles in the writing phase. Even if you announced batman, wonder woman, flash, etc movies today, it's too late. Too much of the universe has been established. 3. Feasibility of starting again. Yes, there's an ownership transfer- which means a lot of projects in early development are getting paused or cancelled. This very much works in favor of starting a new universe, and would help avoid the weird unclean "I'm gonna keep my friends as the same characters" partial reboot of the DCEU into the DCU. In addition, the DCU is in a rough state. Sure, the MCU had Hulk underperform, but Supergirl did worse than morbius. Not to mention the slew of low-viewership and/or heavily controversial R-rated projects. If I was an exec looking at this, I'd say the smart move is to pause everything in production until MoT comes out. If it does great, awesome, greenlight batman and wonder woman. If it doesn't... dig up that schedule they spoke about when the DCEU was first collapsing that was a 5-year plan focused on the trinity. I don't think that's necessarily the case. Paramount isn't the lego group, and studios are always going to want to make a cinematic universe out of anything they can. They're not going to leave the big names on the shelves because Supergirl bombed.

posts.title: LEGO Ideas: Icelandair Boeing 757-200 Hekla Aurora ✈️🇮🇸
posts.text: Hi everyone! I'd like to share my favorite MOC that I have made: a LEGO recreation of Icelandair's iconic Boeing 757-256, TF-FIU, in its unforgettable Hekla Aurora livery! As a longtime aviation fan, I've always loved the combination of the 757's sleek proportions and the Northern Lights design. With the aircraft now retired, I wanted to preserve a little piece of aviation history in LEGO form. The model is nearly 5,000 pieces and measures 108 cm (42.5 inches) long. I've tried to push the build beyond a static display model, incorporating: A completely brick-built Northern Lights livery, using custom plate-stacking patterns rather than large printed pieces or vinyl wraps Folding landing gear Working flaps Opening doors A reinforced Technic spine for structural stability Modular fuselage sections for easier storage I've also avoided large premolded aircraft parts, aiming to create the aircraft's shape using regular LEGO geometry wherever possible. The model was designed in LEGO Studio over many months, and getting the long, slender 757 proportions and the flowing aurora pattern to work together has been a particularly interesting challenge. The project is now live on LEGO Ideas! If you'd like to see it become a set, you can find it here: https://ideas.lego.com/product-ideas/d04b961f-8b50-4bed-a198-4641fa301073 I'd love to hear what fellow builders think, especially about the shaping, structural design, and how well the model captures the original aircraft. Thanks for taking a look! #Airplane #Aircraft #Boeing757 #Icelandair #Model #HeklaAurora #NorthernLights

posts.text: There are many timers in your code. But the Wait block floating around cannot work alone like this, remove it from you code area (put it in the trash bin... you can get it back by clicking on the trash bin after if needed like any other code you remove... Floating blocks can affect the running of a program or not but better maintain your code area clean. Other than that, for me, your code with the after 2 sec timer is working fine. Unless I don't understand what you're trying to achieve... The ON FOR block is an Int.B functionality. The time setpoint you mention in this block is sent to Int.B and the Timer for this block does not execute in blockly but it executes only in Int.B uController. So if you use this ON FOR Block in blockly, blocky will go to next block immediately not waiting. The idea behind this is if you want to run Multiple Outputs with ON FOR all at the same time with different delays. OUT A ON FOR 2s OUT B ON FOR 5s OUT C ON FOR 7s You do not want to wait for each ON FOR to finish before starting the next ON FOR... They must all execute at the same time. That is why you must know that and use your own timer in blockly which duplicate the one in Lego Int.B... The following code does the same thing you did but with only one ON FOR block. of 5 sec total. (Also note the use of SET RIGHT/LEFT rather than ON RIGHT/LEFT) Personnaly, I prefer not to use ON FOR blocks... I do the ON and OFF commands in blockly. Note that the Wait block is a "blocking" block meaning that the main code flow will stop at the wait block until the time as elapsed to the time setpoint. The After Time block in a "non blocking" block. Meaning that you main code flow will immediately go to the next block in your flow. But the After Block will still execute after its time has elapsed. That is why your code works even if the program finishes IMMEDIATELY after you press RUN.

posts.title: Using Claude AI for new ports and translations
posts.text: May be very offtopic, nevertheless I would like to point out that reverse engineering may not be allowed by laws / EULAs of the released software assets from a vendor. I know, I know, this is generally a big topic right now for asking Frontier-Models to reverse-engineer compiled code back into sourcecode - still it may be considered at minimum gray area if not worse. Just because you can, doesn’t mean you should. The other effect I believe people are not understanding (yet): If everybody now starts ordering the frontier models to do rev-engineering, the providers will get the knowledge for real code from plenty of real applications - my assumption is that this may kill the whole (closed) software developement. Just imagine the Frontier models can easily replicate any software at lower costs than the original vendor (Adobe may be the best current example). In my scenario any software development may get considered "not worth it, as it could easily copied from / with AI & killing any expectations for revenue" - even for developing new ideas into software products. That is what is scaring me the most right now.. But I don't want to steal away the topics..

posts.title: LEGO Star Wars Set Discussion 2026 - READ FIRST POST!!!
posts.text: Just for fun (and to illustrate a point), I put together a list of every new minifig each year based on a pre-established canon character, meaning minifigs based on then-upcoming movies and shows don’t count. Spoiler: 2027 sets a new record In some cases, the minifigs only got released a month after the respective movie did, so it’s somewhat disingenuous to count them as pre-established. In those cases, I present both numbers, with and without these characters. I’ll also select the most significant additions each year 1999: 11, all OT. TPM was new and thus doesn’t count. I’d say the entire OT cast that year is significant! 2000: 10, mostly OT. Chewy, Leia, Boba, and Palpy win. 2001: 5, again mostly OT. Watto and the first Stormie are definitely the most important additions. 2002: Only 4 since AotC was new. Yoda and Wicket are the clear winners. 2003: 9, once again mostly OT. Jabba, Lando, and Bib win. 2004: 1, namely Greedo. Weird year 2005: 6, with a mix of OT and PT. Mace Windu, Luminara, Owen, and the Jawas are all worthy additions. 2006: 6, all OT. Tarkin, Dengar, and IG-88 are the standouts. 2007: 6, mostly OT. Veers and Kit Fisto take home the trophy. 2008: 5, mostly PT this time! The year was filled to the brim with TCW sets, which of course don’t count here Besides pre-existing characters like Plo Koon and Ventress that is! The latter is a bit of a strange case as she did exist before TCW, but in now non-canon material. 2009: 10, even split between OT and TCW. Ackbar, Mon Mothma, and Nute Gunray stand out. 2010: 11, with a focus on TCW. Aayla Secura, Cad Bane, and Bossk are the best additions in my eyes. 2011: 20, with lots of TCW additions, but also PT and OT sprinkled in. I’ll pick Panaka, Embo, Ki-Adi Mundi, Eeth Koth, Logray, and Wald. 2012: 15, with a mix of all three again. Noteworthy characters include Gree, Boushh, Even Piell, Oola, and Salacious B. Crumb. 2013: 17, with a healthy mix. My faves are Coleman Trebor, Malakili, Poggle, and Pong Krell. 2014: 11, with a renewed focus on the OT. Highlights include the Bith, Tarfful, and Neyo. 2015: 6, but that makes sense with TFA coming out. Rebels, the OT, TCW, and the PT all got at least one. I’ll go with the Grand Inquisitor, Yularen, and Tarpals. 2016: 20, or 17 when you remove the TFA characters from January. Rebels and TFA got a lot of love. Significant ones are the Fifth Brother, Maz Kanata, Gregor, and Unkar Plutt. 2017: 12, or 9 without the RO ones early in the year. Rebels and ST fans ate well. Thrawn, Snoke, Raddus, and Quarrie are the big ones. 2018: 13, or 6 without the Solo characters from the June wave. I’ll pick Merrick, Wuher, and DJ. 2019: 9, with a mix between OT, ST, and Battlefront. Bail Organa, Iden Versio, Zuckuss, and the Knights of Ren stand out. 2020: 18, or 16 without the new characters from the January TRoS sets. A lot of focus on the OT and ST with Evazan, Garindan, Ponda Baba, and the remaining Knights of Ren, plus Grogu and Greef Karga! 2021: 14, with TCW, TBB, and Mando getting the lion’s share. Highlights include Bo-Katan, the Armourer, Paz Vizsla, Gideon, Todo, and the entire Bad Batch deserving a mention. 2022: 12, with a mix between OT, PT, and Mando. I’ll pick Beru, BD-1, Kuiil, and Taun We. 2023: 5, surprisingly! But yeah, lots of new characters are from Mando S3 and Ahsoka, which don’t count. Morgan Elsbeth, Huyang, and Garven Dreis are the obvious choices. 2024: 18, mostly thanks to the anniversary! Malak doesn’t count as he’s not canon. Characters that do count are Cal Kestis, Saw Gerrera, Kelleran Beq, Darth Jar Jar (sort of, the idea did exist before), and Nien Nunb. 2025: 15, with the ST, Andor, Ahsoka, the OT, and the PT being represented. Highlights include Babu Frik, Bly, Bacara, Lama Su, Dedra Meero, Motti, and Tagge. 2026: 6, which is again rather low, but we can blame M&G for that All of them are from Mando, with the standouts being Carson Teva, Cobb Vanth, and Dr. Pershing. 2027: 0. Nada, nothing, zilch I’m not tryin
